$comment: Violation ratchet for gates whose dead scan root was repaired. A repair REVEALS pre-existing debt; it does not create it. Each entry records the count revealed at repair time — the gate fails only when its count RISES. Lowering a count is a normal commit; raising one is a defect. Entries expire: a baseline that has not dropped within 56 days of `landed` (or of `reaffirmed.date`) fails its gate, because a number that never moves is suppression with extra steps. Mechanism + rationale: src/scripts/_lib/gate_baseline.ts. Decision: AI council 2026-08-02, roadmap road-to-gates-that-can-fail blocker `dead-gate-finding-triage`.

gate-hardening:unhardened-scan-scope.note: Gate scripts under src/scripts (population 233, defined once in _lib/gate_population.ts — see population_correction below for why it is no longer 223) that neither route through _lib/scan_scope nor emit the machine-readable 'scanned:' line WHILE REGISTERED ENFORCED IN gate-coverage.yml WITH A FLOOR — the gates that can still report success over a moved or empty root without saying so. The registration clause was added 2026-08-04 after measuring that all 14 emit-only gates were already registered, so the count did not move (189 → 189): an unregistered 'scanned:' line is read by nobody, which made adding one the cheapest route to a green ratchet AND the route that changes nothing, while padding the manifest is an explicit non-goal. check_gate_coverage itself was converted in the same change rather than being grandfathered. This is a VULNERABILITY count, not a coverage percentage: it measures how much of the original defect class is still reachable, it RISES whenever a new gate is written without a scope assertion, and its target is 0. That direction is the whole point — an adoption-reach metric ('hardened gates must increase') can never regress and would be threshold-lowering wearing a ratchet's clothes (AI council 2026-08-04, anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-5 + openai/gpt-4o, convergent on scope decomposition plus this discriminator). Clearing it is the charter of road-to-gate-hardening-adoption; the 56-day non-stagnation clause applies unchanged, so a number that never drops fails this gate rather than hardening into configuration. NEW ENTRY, not a raised threshold: this records newly-measured pre-existing exposure at first measurement — nothing was loosened.

population_correction.why: The DENOMINATOR was wrong, not the threshold. Three sites defined 'a gate' with three regexes and got 223 / 225 / 232; the ratchet read the narrowest. It counted check_secret_leak.test.ts — a test file, which can never be hardened, so its own target of 0 was unreachable by construction — and it missed 10 real gates (8 skill_*, 2 verify_*), one of which (skill_linter) already carried an enforced floor of 380 in gate-coverage.yml, so the manifest and the ratchet openly disagreed about whether it was a gate. Unifying on src/scripts/_lib/gate_population.ts raised the honest count 189 -> 198; the five conversions in the same PR brought it to 193.
population_correction.not_headroom: A raised baseline is normally how a gate is disarmed, so this entry is falsifiable rather than asserted. Reproduce with: node --import tsx -e "import {list_unhardened_gates, count_gate_scripts} from './src/scripts/check_gate_coverage.ts'; console.log(count_gate_scripts(), list_unhardened_gates().length)" — expect population 233. The 10 newly-visible gates are named in the PR body; none of them was hardened by this change, every one is still counted. A stalled sweep buying itself headroom would show a count rising with no population change and no named entrants.
population_correction.council: AI council 2026-08-04 (anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-5 + openai/gpt-4o, 3 rounds, deep): unify FIRST. Reaching 0 on the narrow population would force deleting the ratchet entry — the roadmap own closure criterion — at the exact moment 10 gates still needed conversion, leaving that work with no ratchet protection. That is a logical impossibility in the roadmap, not a scheduling preference.

check_no_new_legacy_path:hardcoded-scan-.note: Lines under src/scripts/**/*.{ts,mts,mjs} that pass the retired `.agent-src.uncondensed` directory into `path.join(...)` — a filesystem path CONSTRUCTED against the tree ADR-051 abandoned, which is the exact shape of all 14 dead gates. Deliberately narrow so the number is signal, not noise: 236 raw mentions under src/scripts → 147 string-literal lines → 67 path-constructing lines when the pass was written, after exempting src/scripts/_lib/agent_src.ts (the shared resolver, whose job IS owning the constant — gates that route through it survived the move). Detectors holding the literal as data to match, strip, or print are not counted, and no prose, docs, tests or fixtures are read: that full-tree shape was measured at 44 files / 213 hits and rejected as the wrong lint (see the note in check_no_new_legacy_path.ts::find_offenders). Recorded at 58 rather than 67 because Phase 1's scan-root repairs were landing on this branch while the pass was being written and had already removed 9 — a baseline above the truth silently permits new violations. This count goes to ZERO as the remaining repairs land; every repair is a lowering commit. Lowered 56→51 by the road-to-renewal-foundation Phase 1 dead-root sweep (check_always_budget, check_portability, check_references, lint_framework_leakage, lint_agents_md). Lowered 51→49 by the gate-hardening adoption PR: skill_collision_clusters and skill_overlap were repointed at the live skills tree via the shared resolver — two gates that had been reading the retired container and scoring 0 of 288 skills.

audit_user_type_axis.note: One orphan user-type value: `legal`. Five legal-review-prep skills (contract-review, dpa-review, nda-triage, legal-intake-triage, legal-practice-profile) declare `recommended_for_user_types: [legal]`, but there is no `user-types/legal.yml` — the pack shipped an axis value with no user-type definition behind it, and the dead scan root hid it (the audit reported used=0 orphans=0 while reading zero skills; it now reads 288 and reports used=8). Clearing this entry is a product call, not a copy edit: either author `user-types/legal.yml` (tagline, recommended packs, install-path hint) or drop `legal` from those five skills. Not decided here because both options change shipped pack behaviour.

lint_handoffs.note: All 18 are `handoff_tier_mismatch`: a senior-tier skill links to a peer whose frontmatter carries no `tier` (reported as tier='unset') — e.g. build-buy-partner → adr-create, customer-research → po-discovery, gated-reach → threat-modeling. This is a tier-metadata backfill backlog on the LINKED-TO skills, not a broken link. The one genuinely dangling link revealed by the same repair (competitive-positioning → a non-existent ../analyze-reference-repo/SKILL.md; it is a command, not a skill) was FIXED in the repairing commit rather than baselined. Clearing this entry means backfilling `tier` on the linked-to skills, or deciding that `tier: unset` on a link target is not a violation and narrowing the rule.

lint_pack_boundaries.note: Markdown links between source artefacts that cross a pack boundary the source pack's `requires` graph does not reach — revealed when the scan root moved off the deleted packages/ tree to the live corpus (0 -> 753 artefacts scanned). 82 distinct pack pairs across 131 source files; largest single class is engineering-base -> meta (73), skills in a consumer-installable pack citing this package's own maintenance skills. Each is a link that dangles for a consumer who installs the source pack without the target's. Judged real drift rather than an over-strict gate because it is long-tailed — top bucket 22%, no single systematic cause — unlike the lint_artefact_frontmatter case, where one required shape had 0-of-288 adoption. Fix per finding: add the edge to packs.yml requires, retarget the link, or move the artefact.
